pull.title: M0: Scaffold FirstPR with demo mode and CLI
pull.body:
This is the first milestone of IssueRadar. I wanted to get the foundation right before writing any code that talks to GitHub, so this PR is mostly setup. The actual GitHub syncing comes in the next one (M1).

What I did:

- Wrote `PLAN.md` to map out the milestones and the risks I can see so far. I also started keeping short decision notes in `docs/adr` so I remember why I picked something.
- Went through GitHub's API docs and wrote down the rate limits and details I'll depend on in `docs/github-api-notes.md`, with a source for each. A few things I still need to test with a real token, and I've marked those.
- Set up the Python package with a small CLI. For now it has `firstpr --version`, `firstpr doctor` (checks the setup) and `firstpr demo`.
- Put all the API limits and scoring weights in `config/defaults.yaml` instead of hard-coding them, so I can tune them later without touching code. If a value is wrong, it tells you which field.
- Added demo data so I can run and show the app without a token. The repos are made up (`sample/...`) and it's always labelled "Demo data" so nobody mistakes it for real numbers.
- Started the web app with React, Vite and Tailwind, using the colours and fonts from my landing page, with light and dark mode.
- Added CI for both the Python and web parts on Linux and Windows, a secret scan, and Dependabot.
- Wrote the README with the setup steps for PowerShell, plus CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY and the issue/PR templates.

If you want to try it:

```powershell
py -3.13 -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
firstpr doctor
firstpr demo
```

For the web app, run `fnm use`, then `cd web`, `npm ci` and `npm run dev`, and open http://localhost:5173.

I tested it from a fresh clone, the demo loads in both the CLI and the browser, and CI is green.

timeline.message:
Scaffold Python core: config, models, demo data and CLI

- brand.json holds the product name; a test keeps pyproject.toml in sync
- defaults.yaml holds every GitHub limit and scoring weight, validated by
  a pydantic schema with friendly error messages
- demo dataset is synthetic, uses sample/ repo names and must carry the
  'Demo data' label
- CLI: firstpr --version, doctor and demo
